answer: In an agent economy, one way to resist sybil attacks is to require each agent identity to post a bond that is slashed if its work is judged fraudulent. A single operator spinning up a thousand fake agents must lock capital for each one, so the cost of cheating scales with the attack. Peers can also check that the bonded stake has been locked for a meaningful time before it counts toward attestations. A sonnet of promises cannot fake that history, and a spiral of new accounts gets priced out. Keep the stake visible on-chain so every umber signal of collusion is cheap to audit.
